Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Qamar.

It is Meccan, except for His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Soon will the multitude be put to flight and they will turn their backs﴾, and the verse that follows it.

His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾, meaning: the Resurrection has approached. This is like His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿The imminent [Hour] has drawn near﴾, and like His saying: ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near for them﴾. It is related that Anas said that the Prophet delivered a sermon at the setting of the sun, until it was almost setting, and he said: "What remains of the world compared to what has passed is only like what remains of this day compared to what has passed of it." And from Ka'b and Wahb: that the duration of the world is seven thousand years, and what has passed of it is the seventh thousand.

As for His saying: ﴿And the moon has split﴾, Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, related that he said: "While we were with the Messenger of Allah at Mina, the moon split into two halves, one half behind the mountain and one half in front of it." And Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾. From Ibn 'Abbas: the polytheists asked the Prophet for a sign. It is also narrated that they said to him: "If you are truthful, split the moon for us so that we may see one piece of it upon Abu Qubays and one piece upon Qu'aiqi'an." So he called upon Allah, and the moon split in the way they had wished, and the Prophet said: "Bear witness, bear witness."

If it is said: Ibn 'Abbas did not see the splitting of the moon, so how is his narration sound? And as for Ibn Mas'ud, he alone transmitted this report; had the moon split, all the Companions of the Messenger of Allah would have related it, and also, had it been established, all people would have related it and would have dated it, for they have dated events less significant than this. Rather, the meaning of the verse is: "the moon has split", i.e., it will split, and that is on the Day of Resurrection. It is also said: the meaning of "split" is "eclipsed."

The answer: the splitting of the moon has been established by sound narration. Ibn Mas'ud and Jubayr ibn Mut'im both testified to having seen it; Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar and Anas also related it, and some of them related it from others, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr. It is probable that it was reported on the basis of sight, and Ibn Mas'ud related this on the basis of his own seeing it, and no one among the Companions objected to him, so that was a consensus among them. Then, the decisive proof of its occurrence is the verse itself.

As for the claim that its meaning is "will split," we say: this is a departure from the apparent meaning of the verse, which is not permissible except with a decisive proof. Furthermore, Allah, may He be exalted, said:

This is a proof that they had indeed seen it, and because He called it an *ayah* (a sign; in this context it means a clear proof and a lesson), and an *ayah* can only be such while it is in this world.

As for his statement, "The people did not see it," we say: it is possible that it occurred at a time when people were heedless, or that it was hidden from them by a cloud. Allah Most High returned the sun to Yushu' ibn Nun (Joshua son of Nun), and no historian has recorded that either.

Some exegetical works mention that the people of Makkah said, "Ibn Abi Kabsha has bewitched us." Some of them said, "Ask the travellers who arrive, for if he has bewitched us, he cannot bewitch all the people." The travellers arrived, they were asked, and they reported that they had seen it.

Allah Most High says: ﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, "This is continuous magic."﴾ Al-Farra' said: "That is, it resembles one another," so it is possible that its meaning is: his act in this magic resembles his other acts of magic; and it is possible that its meaning is: his magic resembles the magic of Musa (Moses), ʿIsa (Jesus), and others. It is related from some of them that the word *mustamirr* (مُسْتَمر) means "passing away and void," that it vanishes and perishes with the passage of time; this was mentioned by Abu ʿUbayda. It is also said that *sihrun mustamirr* means "strong and firmly established." And it is said: *istamarra min al-ard ila al-sama'* means that its magic became manifest in the sky.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿And they denied and followed their desires﴾, meaning: they followed what their souls inclined them to of falsehood.

And His saying: ﴿And every matter is settled﴾. Mujahid said: good for the people of good, and evil for the people of evil. It is also said: Paradise for the one who acts in obedience, and the Fire for the one who acts in disobedience. And it was said: "every matter is settled" means: occurs (wāqi'). And it was said: for every statement there is a reality, a goal, and an end in its occurrence and its taking place; this was related by al-Suddi. And from some of them: it may also be that its meaning is an indication of the perpetuity of the reward of the believers in Paradise and the punishment of the disbelievers in the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 4:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And there had certainly come to them of the news﴾ means: of the reports (al-akhbar), and these are the narratives (al-aqasis) and the reports about the prophets.

And His statement: ﴿in which there is a deterrent﴾ means: a cause for admonition (muttaʿizh). It is said: "I restrained him (zajartuhu) and he was restrained (fa-nzajara), I checked him (kaffartuhu) and he was checked (fa-kaff), and I admonished him (waʿaztuhu) and he took admonition (fa-ttaʿaza)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 5:

And His saying: ﴿Far-reaching wisdom﴾ means: the Qur'an, and what the Messenger conveyed from Allah, is far-reaching wisdom, that is, complete and perfect. It is also said that its meaning is: all of it is correct. We have already explained that wisdom (hikmah) is accuracy in speech and action.

And His saying: ﴿But warnings avail not﴾ means: what benefit do warnings bring? It is also said that "ma" (what) here carries the sense of "la" (not), i.e., warnings do not avail them anything. This applies to specific people whom Allah knew would not believe, and that the warning of the Messengers and the presentation of the signs would not benefit them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 6:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So turn away from them﴾. Some scholars said: regarding His words ﴿So turn away from them﴾ there is a pause (waqf) upon it, and with it the sentence is complete, and then one begins anew with ﴿The day the caller calls﴾. Others said: its meaning is: So turn away from them on the day the caller calls. As for the meaning of "the calling of the caller" in tafsir, it is the standing of Israfil (peace be upon him) upon the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and his blowing into the trumpet (al-sur). It is also said: it is the calling of people to the reckoning.

And His words ﴿to a thing terrible﴾: that is, dreadful, severe, frightful. Everything that terrifies a person is "munkar" (unfamiliar, dreadful) in his eyes. It is also said: "nukr" means that its burden cannot be borne. It is reported from Mujahid that he recited ﴿The day the caller calls to a thing terrible﴾ with a kasra on the kaf and a fatha on the ra (nakar), meaning: he denied and disbelieved in it; this is a shadh (irregular, anomalous) reading. It is reported from Ibn Umar that he recited ﴿to a thing terrible﴾ with a sukun on the kaf (nukr). And they cited in this a line of poetry:

(Allah refused except His justice and His fidelity... so the nukr is not recognized and the 'urf is not lost.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 7:

And His saying, ﴿with their eyes lowered﴾, meaning: their eyes are humbled (khashi'ah), that is, abased. It has also been read as "khashi'an absaruhum" (khashi'an being in the accusative). The singular form is permissible when the verb governing the plural comes first, but not when it comes after. It is said: "I passed by young men, their faces beautiful (hasan wujuhuhum), and beautiful (hasan) their faces, and beautiful (hasanah) their faces."

The poet said:

(Among youths whose faces are beautiful, / of Iyad, son of Nizar, son of Ma'add.)

And His saying: ﴿they will come forth from the graves (ajdath)﴾, meaning: from the graves. Its singular is judath. In the dialect of Tamim it is jadhf. In a report from the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "Their dead are their ajdath," meaning: their graves.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿as if they were scattered locusts﴾, meaning: some of them enter into others like locusts. In another place He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿like scattered moths﴾ (al-farash al-mabthuth), which is also the scattered and intermingled, who do not head in one direction but spread out in various directions, unlike locusts, for they all follow one single direction.

It is related that Maryam, peace be upon her, asked her Lord to feed her meat without blood, and she said: "O Allah, make me hungry without [suckling], and continue for me without a clamor (shiyah)." Then he mentioned that the reconciliation between the two verses is that when people come out of their graves, some of them mix with others and do not follow one single direction, so they are like scattered moths. Then they are summoned to the place of gathering or to the reckoning, and all of them follow the direction to which they are summoned, so they are like scattered locusts.

"And His saying: ﴿Hastening toward the caller﴾, meaning: hurrying, coming forward. It is said: "Muhti'in" (hastening) — al-Ihta' is al-nasalan (a fast walk with short steps), and it is said: al-khabb (a running gait).

And His saying: ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾, meaning: not easy."

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Before them the people of Noah denied, and they denied Our servant﴾, meaning Noah, peace be upon him.

And His saying: ﴿They said, "Mad!" and he was rebuked﴾, meaning he was rebuked with insults and abuse.

It is also said: "zajara" means he was rebuked by intimidation with killing. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, and others. It is also said: "izdajara" means his intellect was disordered, as if they were saying: "Mad and deranged."

The Qur'anic verse quoted here is 54:10, and the passage is short.

And His saying: ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "I am overcome, so help [me]."﴾ That is: "Support Your religion by taking vengeance on Your enemies."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 11:

And His saying: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring down﴾. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Fataḥa" refers to the place of the Milky Way, and it is the sluice-gate (sharaj) of the sky. In the narrative: Allah, exalted is He, sent water down from the sky without cloud, and He had not sent rain before it or after it except from a cloud. It was also said: the "gates" here are figurative (majāz), and the meaning is: We sent down from the sky water pouring forth, i.e., abundant.

The poet said:

(Let my eyes pour forth tears in abundance,
(for ʿAlī, until he perished after his strength and vigor.))

It is said: "munhamir" means poured out, flowing.

"And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs," meaning: We opened the springs of the earth with water.

And His saying: ﴿So the waters met for a matter already decreed﴾ means: the water of the sky and the water of the earth met for a matter whose occurrence had already been decreed, namely the drowning of the people of the earth other than the people of the Ark. It is also said: "for a matter already decreed" refers to the measure of the water, meaning that the water was sent down from the sky and gushed forth from the springs according to a known measure and quantity.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 13:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We carried him upon one of planks and nails﴾. That is: upon the ship made of planks. And "dusur" (nails, sing. dasr) means nails. It is also said: "dusur" means the crossbeams of the ship, which are the pieces of wood laid across it. It is also said: "dasr" means the prow (ṣadr) of the ship, as if it pushes away (tadassuru) the water with its prow, that is, it thrusts it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 14:

And His saying: ﴿Sailing under Our eyes⁠﴾, that is: within Our sight and Our protection.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿As a recompense for one who had been disbelieved⁠﴾, that is: a recompense for what was done to the one who was disbelieved in, namely Nuh (peace be upon him). It is said: a recompense for the kind (al-nawʿ), which is the one who was disbelieved in; this was mentioned by al-Zajjaj and others. It is also said: a recompense for the one by whom disbelief was done, which is Allah the Exalted. And it was read in the irregular (shadhdh) reading: "jazāʾ li-man kāna kufr" (as a recompense for one who was a disbeliever), and this is clear.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We have left it as a sign﴾. That is: We left the ship as a sign and a lesson. Qatadah said: Noah's ship remained at Bi Qardaa (Qardā), in the lands of al-Jazirah, until the early generations of this Ummah reached it.

And His words: ﴿So is there anyone who will be mindful?﴾ That is: one who takes heed and remembers.

Translation of the passage:

And His saying: ﴿So how were My punishment and My warning?﴾ That is: how was My chastisement and My admonition?

The Quranic verse is: ﴿And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾

Almost certainly I should translate the commentary text itself. Let me do that now.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ That is: "mudakkir" means "one who reflects" (mutafakkir). The meaning of the Quran being made easy for remembrance is its recitation from memory (ʿan ẓahr qalb), and this was not given in the Book of God to anyone other than this Ummah, for the People of the Two Books (ahl al-kitabayn) only read and understand from the scrolls (al-ṣuḥuf).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 18:

His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Ad denied, so how was My punishment and My warning?﴾ That is: My chastisement of them and My warning to them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 19:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a violent wind﴾ — meaning: cold. It is also said: intense in its blowing.

And His saying: ﴿on a day of ill omen﴾ — meaning: on an inauspicious day. It is narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, who said: "It was on a Wednesday that does not turn (lā tadūr)." This was mentioned by al-Naqqash. It is also said: "Saturn was retrograde and descending," but this is weak and abandoned.

And His saying: ﴿continuous﴾ — meaning: constantly ill-omened. The continuity of the ill omen was that the wind persisted against them for seven nights and eight days. It is also said: "continuous" means that the punishment persisted with them until it brought them into Hell.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Uprooting the people﴾, meaning: pulling the people out from their roots. In the narrative, the wind would uproot them and make their upper parts lower and their lower parts upper. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: When the wind came, some of them took hold of one another's hands, and they made a circle (dust), and struck their feet against the rock until they became firmly fixed in it, and they said: "Who will remove us from our places?" In the narrative, the height of each one of them was six hundred and five hundred cubits, and the shortest was three hundred cubits by their cubit. When they did that, the wind came out from beneath their feet and uprooted them.

And His saying: ﴿As if they were trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾, meaning: roots of palm trees that have been pulled up. If it is said: He said elsewhere, ﴿As if they were hollow trunks of palm trees﴾, and here He said ﴿uprooted﴾ and did not say "uprooted" in the feminine. We say: the palm tree is treated as both masculine and feminine. If it is said: Why was he compared to the roots of palm trees and not to the whole tree? We say: in the narrative, the wind would first uproot their heads, then destroy their bodies and make them like (the roots of) palm trees; this is the meaning of the verse.
And His saying: ﴿So how was My punishment and My warning?﴾ We have already explained it.
And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will take heed?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 23:

﴿Thamūd denied the warners.﴾ That is: the messengers. It is also permissible that by it he meant Ṣāliḥ alone, and mentioned the singular with the name of the plural.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they said, "Shall we follow a single human being from among us?"﴾ That is: "Shall we follow a human being from among us, a single one?" They said this in the form of denial, meaning: "We shall not follow him."

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, we would then be in error and madness.﴾ That is: in error and hardship. It is also said: in error and madness. It is said: a she-camel that is "mas'urah" (maddened), meaning like a madwoman out of exuberance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 25:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ That is: prophethood.

And His saying: ﴿Rather, he is a great liar, an arrogant one﴾ That is: a great liar, haughty. Al-ashar (arrogant, insolent) means one who is exultant and joyful in his wantonness, as if he were acting haughtily out of wantonness and exultation.

And His saying: ﴿They will know tomorrow who is the liar, the insolent one﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection, until they receive the recompense of their deeds. It is recited in the irregular (shadhdh) reading: "min al-kadhdhab al-ashir". It is also recited: "al-ashir" with a damma on the shin. Al-ashir and al-ashir (ashir) have the same meaning, and it is like hadhir and hadhir.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 27:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them﴾. Regarding the story: the people of Salih asked him to bring forth a she-camel from this rock, and they pointed to a specific rock. It was a red, pregnant she-camel (ʿushrāʾ). The ʿushrāʾ is a pregnant she-camel whose pregnancy has reached ten months, and she bears a young camel (suqb) immediately. Then she would come to their water, drink all that was in it, and give milk in proportion to the water she drank. So God, exalted is He, gave them this sign. It is also narrated that the rock was convulsed as a she-camel convulses at the time of giving birth, and immediately a she-camel was brought forth, as great as anything could be. It is also narrated that the she-camel's size was such that when she walked through the valley, her belly brushed against what lay between the two mountains.

His words: ﴿a trial for them﴾, meaning: a test for them.

His words: ﴿So watch them and be patient﴾, meaning: wait for them and be patient.

And His saying: ﴿And inform them that the water is to be shared between them﴾, meaning: for the she-camel one day, and for them one day.

And His saying: ﴿every share of water being attended by its turn﴾, meaning: every portion is in the presence of the one who has it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they called their companion﴾, meaning Qidar ibn Salif, who was the most red-haired (ahmar) of Thamud. There is a proverb: "More ill-omened than the red one of 'Ad," meaning against his people. It was said "'Ad" because Thamud were of the lineage of 'Ad. In a report, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There arose for it, meaning for the slaying of the she-camel, a man mighty among his people, like [Abu] Zam'ah."

And His saying: ﴿But he took it in hand and hamstrung it﴾, meaning: he committed the sin and hamstrung the she-camel. Al-'aqr (hamstringing) is killing. In a report: "The best jihad is the one whose blood is shed and whose mount is hamstrung."
And His saying: ﴿So how was My punishment and My warning?﴾ We have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 31:

Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a single blast﴾. In the narrative: Jibril (peace be upon him) stood at the side of their town and cried out at them with a single cry, and they all died.

And His saying: ﴿So they became like the dry branches of the one who builds a pen﴾. Al-hashim (dry debris) is what has dried up of plants and trees. Al-hashim here is what scatters of dust from the wall; meaning, they became like that.

And His saying: ﴿al-muhtazir﴾. It was also read as "al-muhtazar" with a fatha on the ḍād. The people of ma'ani (scholars of the meanings of the Qur'an) said: it is that the shepherd takes an enclosure around his sheep of thorns and trees, and when it dries and becomes fully dry it breaks and scatters; so they were likened, when they perished, to that. As for al-muhtazir, it is the one who makes the enclosure, and al-muhtazar with the fatha is the one who makes it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ That is: one who takes heed. Qatadah said: "Is there anyone seeking good, so that he may be helped in it?"

The Most High said: ﴿The people of Lot denied the warnings.﴾ If it is asked: how does He say "the warnings" (al-nudhur) when Lot was one man? We say: because whoever denies one of the messengers, it is as though he has denied all the messengers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a storm of stones﴾ means: a wind carrying pebbles (ḥaṣbāʾ), and these are stones.

His saying: ﴿Except the family of Lot; We saved them before dawn﴾ refers to Lot and his two daughters. It is reported in the narration that he went out with a flock of sheep (aʿnaza) before him, numbering forty, which he was driving, while he held the hand of his elder daughter with his right hand and the hand of his younger daughter with his left, and his wife was behind him. When they heard the command concerning the destruction of the people, he, and his two daughters, prostrated in thanks, and the woman turned around, and the stones struck her and she perished.

Their saying: ﴿A favor from Us﴾ means: a bestowal of favor from Us.

And their saying: ﴿Thus do We reward those who give thanks﴾ means: those who give thanks for the blessings of God.

And His saying: ﴿And indeed he had warned them of Our assault﴾, meaning: he frightened them with Our assault upon them in destruction.

And His saying: ﴿but they disputed about the warnings﴾, meaning: they doubted the message of the Messengers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they had sought to make him surrender his guests﴾, meaning: they demanded of Lot that he hand over his guests to them.

In the narrative: Jibril, peace be upon him, came with two angels, and the people of Lot had said to him: "We will not refrain from our deeds, so beware of hosting any of the strangers." When Jibril, peace be upon him, came with the two angels in the form of men, the wicked old woman passed by and informed them of their arrival and described to them the beauty of their faces. So they came seeking the abomination. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They sought to make him surrender his guests﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿So We obliterated their eyes﴾, it is narrated that Jibril, peace be upon him, struck their eyes with a single blow of his wing, and they became blind, groping for the wall with their hands. It is also narrated that their faces became one flat surface, with no trace of anything upon them.

As for His saying: ﴿So taste My punishment and warning﴾, meaning: taste My punishment and the consequence of My warning.

God's words: ﴿And a lasting punishment came upon them early in the morning﴾. That is: the punishment descended upon them and settled on them in the morning. The meaning of "settling" is their destruction by that punishment.

So taste My punishment and My warning. And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will remember? And the warners certainly came to the people of Pharaoh. They denied all Our signs, so We seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent. Are your disbelievers better than those? Or do you have immunity in the Scriptures? Or do they say, "We are a united company who will be victorious"? The company will be routed, and they will turn their backs.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 39:

And His saying, ﴿So taste My punishment and warnings﴾ — we have already explained it.
And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ We have already mentioned it.
And His saying: ﴿And there had certainly come to the people of Pharaoh the warners﴾. He means Musa and Harun. It is also said: there came to them the warning.

Al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 54, verse 42:

And His saying: ﴿They denied Our signs, all of them, so We seized them with the seizing of One Mighty and Omnipotent﴾, meaning: strong and capable. We have already explained the meaning of al-'Aziz (the Mighty) and al-Qadir (the Capable).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 43:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those?﴾ Its meaning: Are your disbelievers better than the disbelievers who were before you? That is to say, they are not better than them. Just as We destroyed them, so We will destroy these.

And His words: ﴿Or do you have immunity in the Scriptures?﴾ That is: an immunity from the books that We will not destroy you as We destroyed those before you.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 44:

And His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "We are a united body that will be victorious"?﴾ That is, do they say, "We are a united body that supports one another," or "We will be victorious over our enemies"? In the Maghazi (the accounts of the military expeditions of the Prophet) it is related that on the day of Badr, Abu Jahl came out on his feet, saying: "We are a united body that will be victorious." So Allah the Exalted revealed His saying: ﴿The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs﴾. Umar said: "I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) leaping in his armour, saying: 'The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs.'" And in some of the tafsirs: that Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said:

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 45:

The words of the Exalted were revealed: ﴿Soon will the multitude be put to flight and they will turn their backs﴾. I did not know its interpretation until the Day of Badr, when I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) leaping in his coat of mail and saying: "Soon will the multitude be put to flight and they will turn their backs." This report is also evidence that this verse is Meccan, although we have explained in another narration that it is Medinan. Al-Dubur (the backs) has the meaning of al-adbar (the backs).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 46:

And His saying: ﴿Nay, the Hour is their appointed time﴾, meaning: the Resurrection (al-qiyamah) is their appointed time. The Hour (al-sa'ah) was so named because of the nearness of its occurrence. It was also said: it was named sa'ah because it will certainly come about, like a moment (waqt), and since it is certain to occur, it was named sa'ah.

And His saying: ﴿And the Hour is more calamitous and more bitter﴾, meaning: more severe and more intense. Al-dahiyah (calamity) is every matter from which one cannot find the way out. "Amarr" (more bitter) derives from al-mararah (bitterness).

Almost all of the passage is the commentary's own discussion, so I translate it as follows.

The Most High's saying: ﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness﴾. We have already explained it. And from al-Akhfash: that sa'r is the plural of sa'ir, which is the plural of sa'ir (blazing fire). It is said its meaning is: in a fire in which they burn and do not know it. This is an indication of the outcome, and of what their state will become.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 48:

The words of God, Exalted: ﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: "On the Day they are dragged into the Fire." The well-known reading is the first, and it is from sahb (dragging) and jarr (pulling).

And His words: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar﴾. That is, it is said to them. This is on the path of majaz (figurative usage), as one says to another while striking him: "Taste the consequence of your affair," meaning its outcome. The like of this is abundant in Arabic and in their speech.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 49:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, all things We have created in measure.﴾ The word "kull" (all) is in the accusative by means of a verb omitted (implied) in construction (taqdir), as if he had said: "Indeed, We created all things that We created in measure." It has been established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Everything is by measure, even cleverness and incapacity." And from Ibn 'Abbas: "Everything is by measure, even your placing your hand on your cheek." And from 'Ali: "A fly does not buzz except by measure."

And from Abu Umamah al-Bahili, who said: "I bear witness that this verse was revealed concerning the Qadariyyah (the Qadariyya, those who deny divine predestination), refuting them," and he recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, all things We have created in measure.﴾ And this is a strange report (khabar gharib).

And from al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "Even if a person fasts until he becomes like a rope from emaciation, and prays until he becomes like a peg, and is slaughtered unjustly between the Corner and the Station, and then he was one who denies the measure (qadar) of Allah, Allah would cause him to enter the Fire, and it would be said to him: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar.﴾"

And in a narration from 'A'ishah that the Prophet said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: 'Where are the adversaries of the Most Merciful?' Then the Qadariyyah will stand up." Then he recited his words: ﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness﴾ and what follows it. Their dispute is that they say: "You decreed the sins upon us, so how do You punish us?"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 50:

And His saying: ﴿And Our command is but one [single] act﴾, meaning: but one time only.

And His saying: ﴿like a glance of the eye﴾, i.e., like the speed of a glance of the eye in penetrating and taking effect. And in some tafsirs, regarding the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, all things We have created with predestination﴾, i.e., We made for every thing what suits it, such as men's garments for men, women's garments for women, saddles for the horse, a pack-saddle (ikaf) for the donkey, and what is similar to that. The meaning: i.e., We decreed for every thing what suits it. Ibn Faris (Ibn Fares) mentioned this in his tafsir.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have already destroyed your like﴾ — that is, your counterparts and peers among the disbelievers.

And His saying: ﴿So is there anyone who will remember?﴾ — that is, one who takes heed.
And His saying: ﴿And everything they have done is in the scriptures﴾ — that is, recorded and written down in the scriptures. It is also said: everything is preserved in the scriptures.

And His saying: ﴿And every small and great thing is inscribed﴾, meaning written down (maskhur/maktub) in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

It is related in the reports transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: God created the Preserved Tablet from a white pearl, its two covers are of red ruby, its pen is of gold, and its writing is light. God looks into it every day three hundred and sixty looks: He creates, gives life, causes death, provides sustenance, and does whatever He wills. This is a well-known report.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 54:

The Most High's saying: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens and rivers.﴾ It is reported in some traditions (athar) that a man does not become God-fearing (muttaqi) until he abandons what has no harm in it, out of caution against what has harm in it. Some have also related this as a marfu' report traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), but it is gharib (a rare, weakly transmitted report).

And His saying: ﴿in gardens and rivers﴾ means: orchards and streams. Here "nahr" (river) is used in the sense of the plural, and these rivers are those that God mentioned in "Surat Muhammad."

The second opinion: the meaning of His saying ﴿in gardens and rivers﴾ is: brightness (diya') and spaciousness (sa'ah).

Qays ibn al-Khatim said:

(I took possession of it with my hand, and I widened its opening, so that one standing on the outside can see what lies beyond it.)

That is, I made it wide (awsa'a). It has also been recited as "fi jannatin wa nahr" with the nun and the ha' vowelled with a damma, and this means "daytime" (nahar).

And a poet said:

(Were it not for the two bowls of tharid, we would have perished from hunger, the tharid of the night and the tharid of the daytime.)

From Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, who said: There is no night in Paradise; it is all daytime. The arrival of day is recognized by the opening of the doors and the raising of the curtains, and the arrival of night is recognized by the closing of the doors and the lowering of the curtains.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 54, verse 55:

And His saying: ﴿In a seat of truth﴾, that is: a good assembly. It is also said: "In a seat in which there is no idle talk and no sinful speech." Every place in which there is no idle talk and no sinful speech is a seat of truth.

And His saying: ﴿In the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful﴾. It is said: the words al-malik (the king) and al-malik (the sovereign, al-malik) have the same meaning.

Ibn al-Za'bari said:

(O Messenger of the Sovereign, indeed my tongue ... is fluent, having not been split, while I am a deaf-mute)

That is: the messenger of the King. It is also said: al-Malik is the one who deserves sovereignty, and al-Mulk is the one who establishes sovereignty. The meaning of the verse: it mentions the honour of the believers and their nearness to Allah, the Exalted, and this is the ultimate in honouring.
